Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

SPECIFICATION FOR 
HANDBALLS 



1. Scope — Covers requirements for handballs. 

2. Shape, Dimensions and Mass 

2.1 The handballs shall be spherical in shape with a circumference of: 

a) 58 to 60 cm for Men's handballs, and 

b) 54 to 56 cm for Juniors' and Ladies' handballs. 

2.1.1 A tolerance of 1 percent in the circumference on sphericity shall be allowed. 

2.2 The mass of the handballs with inflated bladder shall be: 

a) 425 to 475 g for Men's handball, and 

b) 325 to 400 g for Juniors' and Ladies' handballs. 

3. Material 

3.1 Leather — The handballs shall be manufactured from butt portion of tight textured cowhide, free 
from flay cuts and grain defects, vegetable, semi chrome or chrome tanned or chrome re-tanned, dyed 
in any colour or pigmented as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. At the end of the 
tanning operation, and before drying, suitable fungicides shall be incorporated for all types of leathers. 
Fungicides used to promote resistance to mould growth in the leather shall be effective and non- 
toxic and their optimum dosage shall be pre-determined (see LB: 3 of IS: 6191-1971 'Methods of micro- 
biological, colour fastness and microscopical tests for leather' ). The material shall show no growth of 
mildew when examined visually after completion of the test in accordance with LB:2 of IS:6191-1971. 
The tanned leather shall be substantially fat-liquored or oiled or both and the surface obtained 
shall be smooth and well set. The leather panels of the handballs shall have a minimum thickness of 
3 mm and minimum tensile strength of 20 580 kN/m 2 (approximately 210 kgf/cm 2 ) when measured on any 
four panels diameterically opposite to each other. It shall have maximum 12 percent temporary 
elongation and maximum 4 percent permanent elongation at 6860 kN/m 2 (approx 70 kg/m 2 ). 

3.1 .1 For testing the tensile strength and temporary elongation, the test methods covered in IS :5914- 
1970 'Methods of physical testing of leather', shall be followed. The double hole stitch strength shall be 
minimum 60 kg/cm thickness of leather when tested according to LP: 8 of IS: 5914-1970. 

3.2 Thread for Stitching 

3.2.1 Linen thread — Rot-proofed and having 5 plies shall be used for stitching. The minimum 
breaking strength of single yarn shall be 4-5 kgf/cm 2 when tested by the method given in IS: 1670-1970 
'Method for determination of breaking load, elongation at break and tenacity of yarns (first revision )'. 

3.2.2 Cotton thread— Shall conform to variety No. 34 of IS: 1720-1978 'Specification for cotton sewing 
threads ( second revision Y \ 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The handballs shall be made from suitable number of panels of shapes capable of giving proper 
sphericity. 

4.2 Colour — The handballs shall be supplied in any single (one) colour only. 

4.3 Stitching — The handballs shall have 24^2 stitches/dm. The stitches shall be well stretched. 
When the handball is inflated to the air pressure, visible threads shall not be more than 2 mm deep from 
the surface of the handball. The panels for the handball shall preferably be cut with self-cutting-cum- 
perforating dies. 

4.4 Mouth — The mouth shall be adequate and permit the nozzle of the inflating pump or needle to be 
accommodated and suitable means shall be provided to deflate the ball. The neck of the bladder shall 
be completely inside the mouth.

5. Marking — Unless otherwise required by the purchaser, each handball shall bear the manufacturer's 
name, initials or trade-mark. 

5.1 ISi Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

6. Sampling — Sampling and criteria for conformity of handballs shall be as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier. The recommended scheme for the same is given in Appendix A. 

7. Packing — Each handball shall first be wrapped in a polyethylene cover and then packed together 
with other balls or according to the instructions of the purchaser. 

APPENDIX A 
( Ciause 6 ) 
SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY OF HANDBALLS 
A-1. Lot 

A-1.1 In any consignment, all the handballs of same dimensions and manufactured from the same raw 
material under similar conditions shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 

A-1 .2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of the standard, samples of balls 
shall be selected and tested separately from each lot. 

A-2. Sample 

A-2.1 The number of handballs to be selected at random from the lot shall depend upon the size of the 
lot and shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1. 

TABLE 1 SAMPLE SIZE AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 
Lot Size 

d) 

Up to 25 

26 to 50 

51 to 100 
101 to 150 
151 to 300 
301 and above 

A-2.2 The handballs in the sample shall be selected at random from the lot and in order to ensure the 
randomness of selection, IS: 4905-1968 'Method for random sampling' may be used. 

A-3. Number of Tests and Criteria for Conformity 

A-3.1 Each handball in the test sample shall first be examined for the material used in the construction 
as given in 3. If any ball In the test sample is found to be made of materials other than those 
specified, all the balls in the lot shall be rejected. 

A-3.2 If the handballs are made out of specified materials then the balls selected according to A-2.1 
and A-2.2 shall be inspected for shape, dimensions and mass according to 2, and workmanship and 
finish according to 4. A bail failing in any one or more of these tests shall be considered as defective. 
The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of the tests as mentioned above, if the 
number of defective balls \n the sample does not exceed the number given in col 3 of Table 1.

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard is in line with the international rules of the game. Due consideration has also been 
given to the current trade practice in the field in the country.
